Do Not travel to:

The provinces of Central Papua (Papua Tengah) and Highland Papua (Papua Pegunungan) due to civil unrest.

healthcare.costForTourists: Bali has good private clinics (BIMC, Siloam). Clinic visit $30-80. Serious cases require evacuation to Singapore. Jakarta has good hospitals. Most of Indonesia outside Bali/Jakarta has very limited facilities.
healthcare.pharmacyAccess: Apotek (pharmacies) in cities. Many medications available OTC. Rural areas and small islands have very limited access.
healthcare.hospitalNotes: BIMC Hospital (Bali) is the go-to for tourists. SOS International Clinic for emergencies. Outside Bali and Jakarta, hospitals are basic. Medical evacuation to Singapore common for serious cases.
healthcare.insuranceAdvice: Travel insurance essential. Medical evacuation coverage critical — evacuation to Singapore costs $20,000+. Bali's healthcare is adequate for minor issues only.

controlledSubstances.note: Indonesia has the death penalty for drug trafficking. Zero tolerance policy. Even small amounts of marijuana can result in 4-12 years in prison.
Restricted. Bring original packaging and prescription.

medications.generalAdvice: Indonesia has extremely strict drug laws — death penalty for trafficking. Carry all medications in original packaging with prescriptions. Bring a doctor's letter for any controlled substance.

scams.name: Money changer short-changing
scams.description: Unofficial money changers use sleight of hand to shortchange you — fast counting, hidden bills, rigged calculators. Some give counterfeit bills.
scams.avoidance: Only use banks or authorized money changers (BMC, Central Kuta). Count your money carefully before leaving the counter. Avoid places advertising rates that seem too good.

scams.name: Motorbike rental damage scam
scams.description: Rental shops claim you damaged the motorbike and demand $200-500 for 'repairs.' Some track you via GPS and send people to confront you.
scams.avoidance: Take photos/video of the bike from all angles before renting. Only rent from reputable shops. Get the rental terms in writing.

scams.name: Temple ceremony donation scam
scams.description: 'Guides' at temples tell you a ceremony requires a large 'donation' of $20-50. Real temple entry fees are 15,000-50,000 IDR ($1-3).
scams.avoidance: Know the official entry fees before visiting. Only pay at the official ticket counter. Decline unsolicited 'guides.'

scams.name: Taxi meter tricks
scams.description: Taxis refuse to use meters or use rigged meters. Some start the meter at a high base rate.
scams.avoidance: Use Blue Bird taxis (reliable, metered) or Grab app. Avoid taxis at tourist traps that refuse meters.

connectivity.simOptions: Telkomsel (best coverage), XL, or Indosat SIM at airports. $3-8 for 30 days with 10-30GB. eSIM via Airalo. Telkomsel has the best coverage on remote islands.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Free WiFi at most hotels, cafes, and restaurants in Bali and Java. Can be slow. Remote islands and rural areas have limited connectivity.
connectivity.bestOption: Telkomsel SIM for best coverage. Buy at airport — registration required (passport photo).

cultural.tipping: Not expected but appreciated. Restaurants: round up or 5-10%. Spa: 10-15%. Tour guides: $5-10. Drivers: $3-5/day.
cultural.dressCode: Cover shoulders and knees at temples (sarong required — usually provided). Modest dress in Muslim areas (Java, Lombok). Bali beach towns are casual.
cultural.greetings: Slight bow or nod. Handshake is common (right hand only). Muslims may not shake hands with opposite gender — follow their lead. 'Selamat pagi/siang/sore/malam' for different times of day.
taboos: Using your left hand (considered unclean — always eat, give, and receive with right hand)
Pointing with your index finger (use thumb)
Public displays of affection in Muslim areas
cultural.haggling: Essential at markets, with drivers, and at souvenir shops. Start at 30-40% of asking price. Not at restaurants, hotels, or shops with price tags.

safety.lgbtSafety: Not illegal nationally (except Aceh province under Sharia law). Bali is tolerant. Java and other Muslim-majority areas are conservative. Avoid public displays of affection.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Generally safe in Bali and tourist areas. Dress modestly outside Bali. Be cautious at night. Use Grab for transport.
safety.notes: Bali is very safe for tourists. Main risks: motorbike accidents (leading cause of tourist injury), petty theft, and monkeys stealing things at Ubud Monkey Forest. Be aware of rip currents at beaches.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: visa on arrival 30 days ($35), extendable once. Some nationalities get 30-day free visa.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: April-October (dry season). Bali: May-September best. Avoid Dec-Mar (heavy rain).
